(Co-)Plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: (Philipp Joachim Vogt von Altensumerau, Freiherr von Praßberg), Ordensmeister of the Order of St John in the German lands.
(Co-)Defendant/intervenor: Mayor and Council of the imperial city of Rothenburg ob der Tauber.
Plaintiff’s procurators: Lic. Johann Adam Bissing (1755); Lic. Damian Ferdinand Haas and (substitute) Lic. Johann Werner (1763); Lic. Damian Ferdinand Haas and (substitute) Lic. Johann Joseph Flach (1775); Lic. Gabriel Niderer and (substitute) Lic. Johann Christoph von Brandt (1777); Lic. Gabriel Niderer and (substitute) (Lic. Friedrich Wilhelm Bi)ssing (1798).
Defendant’s procurators: Dr Johann Jakob von Zwierlein (1755); Dr (Christian Jakob) von Zwierlein (1772); Dr Hans Karl Freiherr von Zwierlein and (substitute) Dr Caspar Friedrich Hofmann (1793); Dr Hans Karl Freiherr von Zwierlein and (substitute) Lic. Johann Wilhelm Buff (1803).
Contemporary subject of dispute: mandatum super constitutione pignoratitia iuncto restitutorio et de nihil amplius moliendo in res et personas impetrantium ut et de non contraveniendo transactioni s. (c.), de non turbando vero in possessione vel quasi iuris vogtetici et satisfaciendo de damnis per pignorationem causatis c. c.
Modern subject of dispute: Dispute over the Vogtei and civil jurisdiction over the plaintiff’s tenant farm at Reichardsroth.
In March 1754, given the considerable debts of Johann Michael Döppert, tenant of the plaintiff’s farmyard at Reichardsroth, Johann Philipp Lamprecht, Amtmann of the Rothenburg Johanniterkommende, had his property inventoried and summoned his creditors. The mayor and council of Rothenburg then ordered Döppert to the town hall, imprisoned him, issued a public summons to his creditors, removed a wagon from his farm, and seized some of his livestock, which the Amtmann intended to sell outside the landwehr.
The plaintiff Ordensmeister saw this as an inadmissible attempt to remove the insolvency proceedings from the Johanniter Order’s jurisdiction: the agreement of May 1605 granted the commandery the Vogtei and jurisdiction in civil matters within its farmsteads. The mayor and council relied on the Imperial Aulic Council’s judgment of 5 November 1554 (see reference no. 7714): the plaintiff’s farm at Reichardsroth lay within their territory and was subject to the imperial city’s high and low authority and jurisdiction. The later agreement granted the Komtur jurisdiction only over minor offences occurring between servants and household staff at the Order’s estates in Rothenburg and Reichardsroth, and gave him no other jurisdiction. Döppert’s creditors had sued at the Rothenburg imperial court in April 1754; there was no Order court where insolvency proceedings could be conducted. Since the plaintiff Ordensmeister was not directly subject to the Empire in respect of the farm in question, and the imperial city’s Vogtei had long been recognized, the attachment order was unaffected.
Instances: 1. Imperial Aulic Council, 1755–1806 (1755–1803).
Attachments to the plaintiff’s petition (Q 4): extracts from Rothenburg Johanniterkommende records concerning appointment of guardians, estate inventories, divisions of inheritances, and decisions on crop damage and livestock purchases, 1629–1743 (nos. 2–11); record of the Rothenburg Johanniterkommende concerning the inventory of the plaintiff’s tenant Johann Michael Döppert’s property at Reichardsroth, 1754, with an extract from an undated lease (nos. 13, 14).
Witness statements before a notary, 1754 (Q 5, 7, 9).
Agreement between Ordensmeister Weipert (von Rosenbach) and the mayors and council of Rothenburg, 1605 (Q 13).
Further attachments to the plaintiff’s petition (filed 20 August 1755): witness statements before a notary, 1755 (nos. 23, 24).
Fief charters of King Ruprecht and Emperor Franz I for the imperial city of Rothenburg concerning the cent court at Reichardsroth, 1401 and 1753 (Q 21, 22).
Records calculating Johann Michael Döppert’s assets and liabilities and the transfer of livestock and household goods, 1754 (Q 26).
Extracts from testimony before an imperial commission, 1541 (see reference no. 7114, Q 16) (Q 33).
File report on the plaintiff’s statements concerning the inclusion of the Order houses and estates at Rothenburg and Reichardsroth within the imperial city’s territory (Q 34), with attachments (Q 35): extract from a grant by spouses Heinrich and Herrad von Hohenlohe to the Johanniter Order of an estate at Reichardsroth (here: Rode), 1253 (no. I); extracts from the Rothenburg citizens’ register, 1425 (nos. II, III); letters from Komtur Hans Konrad von Rosenberg, his brother Hans Dietrich von Rosenberg, and their administrator, and from Generalrezeptor Gottfried Droste to the mayor and council of Rothenburg, 1616–1663 (nos. IV–VIII).
List of jurisdictional acts exercised by the Rothenburg council over members of the Order, 1399–1750 (Q 36), with associated attachments (Q 40): judgment of the Rothenburg city court in the dispute of priest Johann Mettesholz of Leuzenbronn with Komtur Hermann Krantz at Reichardsroth and Rothenburg over an estate at Gailshofen, 1399 (no. 1); extracts from court books concerning marriage and disciplinary court days at Reichardsroth and post- and complaint-court days at Ohrenbach, 1444–1514 (no. 2); extracts from Rothenburg settlement-oath books, 1505–1538, council records, 1565–1743, court books and judge’s-office records with occasional witness statements, 1579–1750, guardianship-office record, 1620, and judge’s-office registers, 1661 and 1726 (nos. 3–7, 12, 16, 22, 24, 26, 31, 47, 52, 58, 63, 66–70, 83, 84, 88–92, 98, 105, 111, 115); correspondence of the Rothenburg mayor and council with the administrator of the Franciscan monastery there, Johanniter Ordensmeisters, komturs, and administrators, the Brandenburg-Ansbach government, its subordinate Amtmann at Uffenheim, and Comburg dean Erasmus Neustetter gen. Stürmer, 1545–1750 (nos. 8–11, 13, 14, 17–21, 27, 28, 33–46, 48–51, 53–57, 59–62, 64, 65, 71, 73–81, 85–87, 93–97, 100–104, 106, 107, 109, 110, 112–114); agreement concerning the killing of Rothenburg citizen Emerich Neurodt by the Grand Bailli and Komtur Hans Georg von Schönborn in 1572, concluded in 1582 (no. 15); witness statements before a notary, 1602 (no. 29); bond by Johann Friedrich Hund von Saulheim, Generalrezeptor in the Upper German lands and Komtur at Rohrdorf and Dätzingen, concerning delivery of the estate of the Rothenburg Komtur Valentin von der Hees, 1602 (no. 32); liquidation record of the Landvogtei im Gau concerning assessment of two plaintiff’s field fiefs held by the innkeeper at Reichardsroth, 1687, and agreement between the mayor and council and Komtur Otto Hermann Freiherr von Merveldt at Rothenburg concerning collection of the Turkish tax on those field fiefs, 1694 (nos. 72, 82); medical report on injuries resulting from an accident at the Johanniterhof at Reichardsroth, 1734 (no. 99); certificate of the Rothenburg chancery concerning inspection of the church at Reichardsroth, 1747 (no. 108).
Further attachments to the exception pleading (Q 38, Lit. Q–Z; Q 39, Lit. A2–G3): file report on the Imperial Aulic Council proceedings between the two parties concerning the travelling wagon and other points of dispute (see reference no. 7114) (Lit. Q), with Rothenburg council records, 1533–1534, and correspondence between the mayor and council of Rothenburg, their Imperial Aulic Council procurator Simeon Engelhardt, and Ordensmeister Johann von Hattstein, 1535–1541 (Q 37, nos. 1–6, 16); correspondence on the occasion of the 1605 agreement (Lit. R–T); tenancy charter issued by administrator Johann Philipp Lamprecht to Johann Michael Döppert, 1742 (Lit. Z); extracts from correspondence of the Rothenburg mayor and council with the provincial chapter of the Johanniter Order, 1603, Wilhelm von der Hees as heir of Komtur Valentin von der Hees, 1614, and Johanniter komturs and administrators at Rothenburg, 1628–1754, as well as from council, court, and guardianship records, 1620–1754, with some attachments (Lit. A2, B2, D2–I2, M2–G3); entry by Amtmann Lamprecht, who described himself as “Consiliarius et Satrapa,” in the album of a travelling Arab, 1749 (Lit. L2).
Guardianship account of the plaintiff’s farm tenant Erasmus Pfulling at Reichardsroth for Kunigunde Rüdinger, daughter of the plaintiff’s forester and shepherd Hans Rüdinger of Reichardsroth and now wife of baker Martin Hirt of Wallmersbach, 1625/26 (Q 43).
Notarial instrument, 1755, with several documents concerning the estate and insolvency matters of the plaintiff’s tenant Franz Leopold Dedel at Reichardsroth, 1720/21, in particular a certificate by sworn intermediary Jakobina Albig of Rothenburg concerning the sale of the deceased’s movable property, 1721, and a list of creditors, 1720 (Q 44).

Contents/insertions: Process beginning register: 1755.
